output.classification_reasoning: The primary symptom is a replication lag of 450 seconds on a database replica (replica-02) for the order-service, indicating that the underlying data store is not keeping up with writes. The lag affects secondary telemetry and impacts 800 users for 37 minutes, suggesting the issue is beyond a simple transient glitch but does not require a full architectural redesign, placing it in the moderate complexity tier. The failure likely involves database replication configuration, resource contention, or write load spikes, all of which are typical moderate‑complexity database incidents.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has root or ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us-east-1.

remediation_steps.title: Enforce Write‑Freeze and Promote Read‑Replica
remediation_steps.description: Activate a write‑freeze on the primary database, then promote replica‑02 to become the new primary to eliminate replication lag.

remediation_steps.title: Reboot Original Primary Node
remediation_steps.description: Perform a graceful reboot of the former primary node to clear any stuck processes, then re‑attach it as a read‑replica.
verification: EC2 instance status transitions to running

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit

commands: kubectl exec -n order-service $(kubectl get pod -l app=order-service -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- curl -sSf http://localhost:8080/healthz

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert promotion, restore original primary as write source, and cancel write‑freeze. All actions are idempotent and can be undone without data loss.
